text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- The number of frauds detected in Portugal, relating to the use of EU agricultural and structural funds, was the highest in the European Union and totalled 3.5 billion escudos, an EU report said.

- Employment Minister Maria Joao Rodrigues said a programme to create jobs set up a year ago had been a success. She regretted that annual talks between trade unions and employees focused mainly on salaries, neglecting companies' competitiveness and professional training.
- A new space to shelter pilgrims from bad weather will be built at the Fatima sanctuary in the next few years.

- The overhaul of Portugal's creaking social security system should depend on individual contributions earning interest, with an increased participation by the private sector, a study by the Managers' Forum said.

- Employment programmes will be launched this month in the clothing sector, in order to improve the competitiveness of textiles companies via modernisation and a more efficient use of human resources, Employment Minister Maria Joao Rogrigues said.
- The market capitalisation of Lisbon's bourse has risen by 225 billion escudos following an announcement that from December it will be included in Morgan Stanley's index of developed markets.
- Portugal's banking group BCP was in talks with two Brazilian financial institutions as it sought investment opportunities in South America, BCP chairman Jorge Jardim Goncalves said.
